bug_semantics: GitPython's IndexFile.checkout() and TagReference.create() each accept **kwargs and forward them, unguarded, into git checkout-index and git tag. Git.cmd.transform_kwargs turns prefix=<path> into --prefix=<path> (checkout-index prepends that path to every blob it writes, including absolute destinations and -f overwrites) and F=<file>/file=<file> into -F/--file (git tag stores the file bytes as the annotated tag message, which GitPython returns in-band via TagReference.tag.message). Neither call site had allow_unsafe_options nor Git.check_unsafe_options, so caller-influenced kwargs were a direct filesystem write/read primitive. CVE-2026-73620 / vendor GHSA-3f7w-8rr8-f37f; affected < 3.1.57; CVSS 8.1 (overwrite). A later positional TagReference.create bypass of the kwargs-only guard is a different advisory (GHSA-3wxw-xv34-2frg), not this case.
flaw_origin: The executable sinks were first written as intentional git-option passthroughs in 2009 by Sebastian Thiel, before any unsafe-option policy existed. TagReference.create first executed repo.git.tag(*args, **kwargs) in 1047b41e2e925617474e2e7c9927314f71ce7365 (2009-10-23), replacing a same-day NotImplementedError stub; IndexFile.checkout independently first executed self.repo.git.checkout_index(..., **kwargs) three days later in 0ef1f89abe5b2334705ee8f1a6da231b0b6c9a50. Later package splits (af32b6e0, dec46631) only moved the same lines. check_unsafe_options (2022) is per-call-site and never reached these two APIs until the 2026 fix. BIC is the earlier named-site first-write 1047b41e; the checkout first-write is the same human author and does not change attribution.

Vendor advisory + NVD/VulnCheck: unguarded kwargs in IndexFile.checkout() -> git checkout-index --prefix (arbitrary overwrite) and TagReference.create() -> git tag -F/--file (in-band file read). PoC: index.checkout(prefix="/tmp/target_dir/", a=True, f=True) and TagReference.create(..., a=True, F="/etc/passwd").

transform_kwargs at the 2009 BIC already mapped single-letter kwargs (F=path -> -Fpath) and long kwargs (prefix=path -> --prefix=path) in lib/git/cmd.py; Git.__getattr__ forwards checkout_index/tag through _call_process. Path-taking git options therefore worked as soon as the high-level APIs forwarded **kwargs.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-73620 is a published (not withdrawn/rejected) path-traversal issue. GitPython forwards caller **kwargs into git without a per-site unsafe-option guard at IndexFile.checkout (git checkout-index --prefix overwrite) and TagReference.create (git tag -F/--file in-band read). That matches the vendor advisory GHSA-3f7w-8rr8-f37f, the 3.1.57 changelog, and the unique hunks in 3af0c251. GitPython's kwargs-to-CLI transform already existed in 2008-2009, so the high-level passthrough is the first-write of the attack path. BIC hunt used git log -L on git/index/base.py and git/refs/tag.py, then walked through the 2010 package-split commits into lib/git/index.py and lib/git/refs.py, then git log -S for checkout_index and repo.git.tag(*args, **kwargs). The smallest commit that first wrote an executable named sink is 1047b41e (TagReference.create implementation). Its immediate parent still has only the NotImplementedError stub from 2c23ca3c, verified by git show and git grep. IndexFile.checkout is an independent first-write three days later (0ef1f89a) of the same unguarded-kwargs class; that commit is also human Sebastian Thiel, is not a move/squash, and is absent at its parent, but it is not the earliest named-site first-write. Later splits, pep8/black, and 275c37f6 (message-kwarg cleanup) are refactors, not BICs. The 2022 check_unsafe_options helper is opt-in per call site and did not introduce these sinks. AI is judged only on 1047b41e: no commit-object AI authorship, co-authorship, Generated-with, or bot identity. Fix-side GPT 5.6 authorship on 3af0c251 is ignored. Closed NOT_AI with BIC 1047b41e and direct fix 3af0c251.
